content:
Liquid Glass made its debut on iOS earlier this year, and WhatsApp is now working to extend the design to more interface elements. Here are the details.

Liquid Glass is coming to the WhatsApp drawing editor and video player

If the following sounds familiar, bear with us: WhatsApp is working to extend its Liquid Glass redesign to more parts of the app.

Earlier this year, WhatsApp finally rolled out its first wave of Liquid Glass changes more broadly after more than six months of testing.

At the time, the WhatsApp parent company was also exploring applying the new design to elements like the voice message player, message reactions, and context menus, though those changes were only in a beta version of the app at the time.

According to WABetaInfo, the latest iOS beta of WhatsApp shows the company is preparing to apply the Liquid Glass visual style to more interface elements, including the drawing editor and the video player progress bar.

WABetaInfo reports:

It's worth noting that although some 9to5Mac readers frequently say their iPhones have not yet received the first wave of Liquid Glass updates, the latest news shows Meta continuing to adopt this new visual language, including on macOS and iPadOS in addition to iOS.

Speaking of this latest news, WABetaInfo noted that "this feature is still in development and is not yet available for testing."
